The core operator is a hierarchical Poisson regression with exposure offset, modeling shot attempts as a function of team, area, shot type, and season. The model decomposes variation into fixed and random effects, allowing for league-wide comparisons while adjusting for pace and exposure. The fixed effects include intercept, season, court side, and shot type. Random effects include team-specific deviations, area-specific deviations, team×area interactions, team×side interactions, and shot-type-specific slopes. The model uses INLA for fast posterior inference, yielding log-rate contrasts and spatial bias summaries. The failure mode occurs when the Poisson assumption breaks down due to overdispersion or when exposure is misestimated. The model is robust to prior specification, with high Kendall’s τ correlations across priors. It is adaptable to NFL data by mapping play types to shot types and field zones to spatial regions.
